statistical_contract.interpretation: The residual interval is estimate plus/minus 1.95996 combined standard deviations under the adopted summary assumptions. It is not a rigorous physical truncation envelope, a probability that a theory is true, or a new nuclear-network computation.

source_caveats: The retrieved 2604.16600 HTML Table 1 prints Planck 100 omega_b as 2.337, inconsistent with its equation (3) and original Planck value 2.237. This input uses original Planck and equation (3); it does not silently repair the external table or recompute a prediction from 2.337.
D/H was not a fitted datum in the selected nuclear-rate or Planck baseline calibration, but shared theoretical assumptions, including the Planck BBN helium relation, remain.

All three prediction errors are the published 2026 Table 2 summaries, already marginalized over the same Planck omega_b uncertainty. The 0.029 error in equation (12), which fixes omega_b, is not used.
Different rate methodologies share inputs and are shown side by side. They are not independent measurements to average or alternatives from which to choose a convenient pass.
This adopts the standard P981 BBN branch. No claim is made that the B993 sigma state and portal history have been matched to this cosmological window.
